skill_drafts.name: Maven Project Initialization
skill_drafts.description: Quick-start workflow to set up a new Maven project from scratch, covering project structure, archetype selection, and initial configuration within 5–30 minutes.
skill_drafts.objective: Initialize and configure a Maven project ready for build
applicable_signals: Onboarding a developer to Maven basics
Need to establish standard project structure
contraindications: Modifying an existing project's build configuration
Troubleshooting build failures
Adjusting dependency management in an active project
workflow_steps: Select or identify an appropriate Maven archetype for the project type
Apply the archetype to generate the project skeleton
Verify standard directory layout is created (src/main/java, src/test/java, etc.)
Review and validate the generated pom.xml
Confirm project is ready for initial build
triggers: Starting a new Maven project or onboarding a developer to Maven basics
constraints: Archetype selection must match intended project type
Standard directory layout must be preserved
pom.xml must be syntactically valid before handoff
output_contract: A Maven project with standard directory layout, pom.xml, and verified archetype applied; project is ready for dependency declaration and build execution

metadata.prompt: Follow the Maven Getting Started guides to initialize a new project. Select an appropriate archetype, apply it to create the standard directory layout, and verify the pom.xml is correctly generated and ready for build.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Dependency Resolution
skill_drafts.description: Workflow to declare, manage, and resolve project dependencies using Maven's dependency mechanism, including optional dependencies and exclusions.
skill_drafts.objective: Manage and resolve project dependencies correctly
applicable_signals: New library or framework requirement identified
contraindications: Do not use for resolving transitive dependency conflicts at runtime
Do not use for debugging repository connectivity issues
Do not use for managing repository mirrors or authentication
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify the dependency to add or modify', 'detail': 'Determine groupId, artifactId, and version from the library documentation or Maven Central Repository'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Declare the dependency in pom.xml', 'detail': 'Add a <dependency> block in the <dependencies> section with groupId, artifactId, and version'}

{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply optional or exclusion rules if needed', 'detail': 'Mark dependency as <optional>true</optional> if it should not be transitive, or add <exclusions> to block unwanted transitive dependencies'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify dependency resolution', 'detail': 'Run Maven dependency tree command to confirm all dependencies resolve correctly and no conflicts remain'}
triggers: Adding a new dependency to a Maven project
Updating an existing dependency version
Excluding transitive dependencies to resolve conflicts
Marking a dependency as optional
constraints: pom.xml must be valid XML
Dependency coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) must be correct
Maven must have access to configured repositories
cautions: Excluding too many transitive dependencies may break functionality
Optional dependencies still require explicit declaration in dependent projects
Version conflicts in transitive dependencies may require additional exclusion rules
output_contract: pom.xml with correctly declared dependencies, optional flags, and exclusion rules; successful dependency tree resolution with no unresolved or conflicting dependencies

metadata.prompt: Use this skill when you need to add, update, or configure dependencies in a Maven project. Follow the dependency mechanism to declare dependencies in pom.xml, apply optional flags when appropriate, and use exclusion rules to prevent unwanted transitive dependencies. Verify the dependency tree resolves correctly after configuration.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Build Lifecycle Execution
skill_drafts.description: Execute Maven build phases in proper sequence, understanding phase dependencies and orchestrating the complete build lifecycle from compile through deploy.
skill_drafts.objective: Execute Maven build phases in proper order with all prior phases completed
applicable_signals: User initiates mvn command with lifecycle phase target
Build requires validation of phase execution order
Downstream artifacts depend on prior phases completing
contraindications: Configuring individual plugin goals or plugin-specific behavior
Debugging plugin execution failures or plugin parameter issues
Customizing site generation or documentation build steps
workflow_steps: Identify the target lifecycle phase (compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy)
Confirm all prerequisite phases will execute in order
Execute the Maven command targeting the desired phase
Monitor phase completion and artifact generation
Verify all expected build artifacts are produced
triggers: Running a Maven build from command line or CI/CD pipeline
Understanding phase dependencies before customizing build order
Need to execute specific lifecycle phases or full build sequence
constraints: Phases must execute in Maven's defined sequence
All prior phases in the lifecycle must complete before later phases
Phase execution is atomic within the lifecycle context
cautions: Skipping phases may result in incomplete builds or missing artifacts
Phase execution order cannot be reordered; it is fixed by Maven's lifecycle definition
output_contract: Successful execution of the requested lifecycle phase(s) with all prior phases completed; build artifacts generated and available for downstream use or deployment.

metadata.prompt: Invoke this skill when you need to run a Maven build and ensure all lifecycle phases execute in the correct order. Maven's build lifecycle consists of phases that must run sequentially: validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, and deploy. Use this skill to understand which phases are executed, their dependencies, and how to target specific phases or the full lifecycle.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Project Setup and Configuration
skill_drafts.description: Establish a Maven project structure, configure the POM file, and apply build profiles. Use this when initializing a new Maven project or reconfiguring an existing one.
skill_drafts.objective: Set up and configure a Maven project with correct POM and profile settings
contraindications: Troubleshooting runtime errors
Debugging plugin execution during active builds
Modifying plugin behavior mid-build cycle
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create or verify Maven project directory structure', 'details': 'Ensure src/main/java, src/test/java, src/main/resources, and src/test/resources directories exist; place pom.xml at project root'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Define POM project coordinates and metadata', 'details': 'Set groupId, artifactId, version, name, description, and packaging type in the POM'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Configure dependencies in POM', 'details': 'Add required dependencies with scope (compile, test, provided, runtime) and version specifications'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Set up build profiles', 'details': 'Define profiles for different build scenarios (e.g., dev, test, prod) with activation conditions and profile-specific configurations'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Configure plugins in POM', 'details': 'Add and configure plugins for compilation, testing, packaging, and other build phases'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Review Settings descriptor', 'details': 'Verify repository URLs, credentials, and local repository path in settings.xml'}
{'step': 7, 'action': 'Validate POM and settings', 'details': 'Check XML syntax and structure; run mvn validate to confirm POM correctness'}
triggers: Starting a new Maven project
Migrating an existing project to Maven
Reconfiguring project structure and build profiles
constraints: POM file must be valid XML
Project coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) must be defined
Directory structure must follow Maven conventions
cautions: Ensure all dependencies are available in configured repositories before proceeding to build
Validate profile activation conditions to avoid unintended build variations
Review plugin versions for compatibility with the target Java version
output_contract: Valid POM file with correct project descriptor, profiles, and plugin configurations ready for build execution. The project structure conforms to Maven conventions, all dependencies are declared, and the POM passes validation.

metadata.prompt:
Follow these steps to set up and configure a Maven project:
1. Create or verify the project directory structure with src/main/java, src/test/java, and pom.xml at the root.
2. Define the POM file with project coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version), packaging type, and dependencies.
3. Configure build profiles in the POM to support different build scenarios (e.g., development, testing, production).
4. Set up plugin configurations in the POM for compilation, testing, and packaging.
5. Review the Settings descriptor to ensure repository and credential configurations are correct.
6. Validate the POM syntax and structure before proceeding to build execution.

skill_drafts.name: Maven Build Lifecycle Execution
skill_drafts.description: Execute Maven build phases and manage phase transitions in correct sequence. Use this skill when running builds, understanding build lifecycle flow, or coordinating phase execution.
skill_drafts.objective: Execute Maven build lifecycle phases in correct sequence and produce expected build artifacts
applicable_signals: Maven project ready for compilation or packaging
Artifact production expected at specific lifecycle stage
contraindications: Do not use when developing custom Maven plugins
Do not use for repository access configuration
Do not use for Maven settings or profile management
workflow_steps: Verify Maven project structure and POM validity
Identify target build lifecycle phase
Execute Maven build command with appropriate phase
Monitor phase execution sequence
Verify expected artifacts are produced
triggers: Caller needs to run a Maven build
Build phase order must be managed or verified
Build lifecycle flow understanding is required
constraints: Maven project structure must be valid
POM file must be present and well-formed
Build phases must be executed in documented lifecycle order
cautions: Phase execution order is strict; skipping phases may produce incomplete artifacts
Ensure dependencies are resolved before execution phases
output_contract: Build completes through intended lifecycle phases with expected artifacts produced and available for downstream use

metadata.prompt: Invoke this skill when you need to execute Maven build phases in the correct order. The skill guides phase sequencing and ensures build artifacts are produced as expected. Do not use this for plugin development, repository configuration, or Maven settings management.

skill_drafts.name: Plugin Development Setup
skill_drafts.description: Establish and configure a Maven plugin development environment, including project structure, dependencies, and testing infrastructure for custom plugin creation.
skill_drafts.objective: Initialize a reusable Maven plugin development project
contraindications: Debugging an existing plugin
Resolving runtime plugin conflicts
Troubleshooting plugin execution issues
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create Maven plugin project structure', 'detail': 'Use Maven archetype or manual setup to establish the plugin project layout'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Integrate Mojo API', 'detail': 'Add Mojo API dependencies and configure plugin descriptor'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Configure plugin dependencies', 'detail': 'Set up required libraries and Maven plugin API dependencies in pom.xml'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Establish test harness', 'detail': 'Prepare testing infrastructure for development versions of plugins'}
triggers: Starting a new Maven plugin project
Onboarding a developer to plugin development
Establishing a plugin development environment for the first time
constraints: Maven must be installed and configured
Java development environment must be available
Access to Maven Repository Centre for dependency resolution
cautions: Ensure plugin descriptor is correctly configured before testing
Verify Mojo API version compatibility with target Maven version
Test harness must be validated before proceeding to plugin implementation
output_contract: Functional Maven plugin project structure with Mojo API integrated, dependencies configured, and test harness ready for plugin development and validation

metadata.prompt: Initialize a Maven plugin project by setting up the project structure, integrating the Mojo API, configuring dependencies, and preparing a test harness. Follow the Plugin Development guide to establish the foundation for custom plugin creation.

skill_drafts.name: Plugin Prefix Resolution
skill_drafts.description: Resolve and configure Maven plugin prefixes to enable short-form plugin invocation (e.g., mvn myprefix:goal) in command-line and POM contexts.
skill_drafts.objective: Map plugin artifact to a short invocation prefix
applicable_signals: Configuring a new plugin for end-user invocation
Setting up plugin short-form command aliases
contraindications: Using fully qualified plugin coordinates (groupId:artifactId:version:goal)
Internal plugin-to-plugin calls that bypass prefix resolution
Plugins already invoked via fully qualified names in build automation
triggers: Configuring a new plugin for end-user invocation or troubleshooting unrecognized plugin prefix errors
constraints: Plugin must be registered in Maven repository or local repository
Prefix mapping must be defined in plugin metadata or POM configuration
Short-form invocation requires Maven to resolve prefix from repository metadata
output_contract: Plugin prefix registered and verified; short-form invocation command executes without prefix resolution errors.

metadata.prompt: To resolve a plugin prefix: (1) Identify the plugin's groupId and artifactId. (2) Define or verify the prefix mapping in the plugin's metadata or POM configuration. (3) Test the short-form invocation command to confirm the prefix resolves correctly. (4) If resolution fails, check plugin repository metadata and local Maven settings for prefix registration.

skill_drafts.name: Local Repository JAR Installation
skill_drafts.description: Install third-party or custom JAR files into the local Maven repository with correct groupId, artifactId, and version metadata for project dependency resolution.
skill_drafts.objective: Register a JAR artifact in the local repository
applicable_signals: Adding a non-Central Repository JAR to project dependencies
Integrating legacy, proprietary, or locally-built artifacts
Resolving missing artifact errors for unavailable remote sources
contraindications: Artifact is already available in Central Repository
Artifact is available in a configured remote repository
Standard dependency declaration in POM is sufficient
workflow_steps: Identify the JAR file path, groupId, artifactId, and version
Execute mvn install:install-file with -Dfile, -DgroupId, -DartifactId, and -Dversion parameters
Verify artifact appears in local repository at ~/.m2/repository/[groupId]/[artifactId]/[version]/
Add dependency declaration to project POM and confirm resolution without errors
triggers: Adding a non-Central Repository JAR (legacy, proprietary, or local build) to project dependencies
constraints: JAR file must exist and be accessible at specified path
groupId, artifactId, and version must be provided and valid
Local repository directory must have write permissions
cautions: Ensure groupId and artifactId match project naming conventions to avoid resolution conflicts
Verify JAR integrity before installation to prevent runtime classpath errors
output_contract: JAR file installed in local repository at correct hierarchical path; POM dependency declaration resolves without download errors; artifact is available for project compilation and runtime classpath

metadata.prompt: Use the Maven install:install-file goal to register a JAR artifact in the local repository. Provide the JAR file path, groupId, artifactId, and version. Verify the artifact is placed at the correct path in the local repository and that subsequent POM dependency declarations resolve without download errors.

skill_drafts.name: Install Third-Party JAR to Local Repository
skill_drafts.description: Procedure to add external JAR files into the local Maven repository for project dependency resolution. Use when integrating non-standard or proprietary libraries that are not available in remote repositories.
skill_drafts.objective: Register external JAR artifact in local repository
applicable_signals: Build failure due to missing artifact in Central Repository
Requirement to use offline or air-gapped dependency
Integration of vendor-supplied or custom JAR
contraindications: Artifact already available in Central Repository
Artifact should be deployed to shared remote repository for team access
Dependency is managed by a corporate artifact repository
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Identify JAR metadata', 'detail': 'Determine group ID, artifact ID, version, and packaging type (jar) for the third-party library.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Execute install:install-file goal', 'detail': 'Run Maven install:install-file with -Dfile, -DgroupId, -DartifactId, -Dversion, and -Dpackaging parameters.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify local repository indexing', 'detail': 'Confirm the JAR appears in the local repository directory structure (typically ~/.m2/repository).'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Declare dependency in pom.xml', 'detail': 'Add a <dependency> block with matching group ID, artifact ID, and version to the project pom.xml.'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Test build resolution', 'detail': 'Run mvn clean compile or mvn dependency:resolve to confirm the dependency is resolved from local repository.'}
triggers: Third-party JAR unavailable in remote repositories
Local-only dependency required for project build
Proprietary or non-standard library integration needed
constraints: JAR file must be physically available locally
Group ID, artifact ID, and version must be known or inferred
Local repository must have write permissions
cautions: Local-only installation does not share the dependency with team members; consider remote deployment for shared use.
Verify JAR integrity and source before installation to avoid security risks.
output_contract: JAR file indexed in local repository; project build resolves dependency without download attempts; dependency declaration in pom.xml matches installed artifact metadata.

metadata.prompt:
To install a third-party JAR to the local Maven repository:
1. Obtain the JAR file and identify its group ID, artifact ID, and version.
2. Use the Maven install:install-file goal to register the JAR in the local repository.
3. Verify the JAR is indexed and accessible to the project build.
4. Update project pom.xml with the corresponding dependency declaration.
5. Run a test build to confirm the dependency resolves without download attempts.

skill_drafts.name: Deploy Third-Party JAR to Remote Repository
skill_drafts.description: Procedure to publish external JAR files to a shared remote Maven repository for team-wide access. Use when making proprietary or third-party libraries available across multiple projects or developers.
skill_drafts.objective: Publish external JAR artifact to shared remote repository
applicable_signals: Artifact not available in Central Repository
contraindications: Artifact already published in Central Repository
Local-only integration is sufficient
No remote repository access or credentials available
Artifact licensing prohibits redistribution
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify artifact coordinates', 'detail': 'Confirm groupId, artifactId, and version are defined and follow naming conventions'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure repository credentials', 'detail': 'Set up authentication in Maven settings.xml or equivalent for target remote repository'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Execute deployment', 'detail': 'Use Maven deploy command or repository management tool to publish JAR to remote repository'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify accessibility', 'detail': 'Confirm artifact is resolvable by dependent projects via dependency declaration'}
triggers: Third-party JAR must be shared across team
Centralized artifact distribution required
Multiple projects need access to same external library
constraints: Remote repository must be accessible and authenticated
Artifact must have valid Maven coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version)
Deployment credentials must be configured in settings.xml or equivalent
Repository must support artifact deployment
cautions: Verify artifact licensing before deploying to shared repository
Ensure version numbering follows team conventions to avoid conflicts
Test artifact resolution from dependent projects after deployment
Document repository location and access requirements for team
output_contract: JAR artifact published to remote repository and accessible to all team members via dependency declaration. Artifact is discoverable and resolvable by Maven dependency resolution.

metadata.prompt: Deploy a third-party JAR artifact to a shared remote Maven repository. Ensure the artifact is properly configured with coordinates (groupId, artifactId, version) and that authentication credentials are set up for the target repository. Verify that all team members can resolve the artifact via dependency declaration after deployment.

skill_drafts.name: Configure Multiple Repository Sources
skill_drafts.description: Setup and management of multiple Maven repositories (local, remote, mirrors, proxies) to resolve dependencies from diverse sources. Establishes a multi-source dependency resolution strategy when projects require artifacts from multiple repository endpoints or need fallback resolution paths.
applicable_signals: Build fails with artifact not found from single repository
Need to route requests through proxy or mirror
Requirement to balance load across multiple repository endpoints
Security or access control requires repository selection logic
contraindications: Single repository is sufficient for all project dependencies
No network constraints or failover requirements
No security or access control requirements
Build environment has no external repository access
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Define multiple repository endpoints', 'detail': 'Add repository entries to Maven settings or POM with distinct IDs, URLs, and optional authentication credentials'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure repository priority and fallback order', 'detail': 'Establish the sequence in which Maven will attempt to resolve artifacts from each repository'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Apply mirror rules if needed', 'detail': 'Define mirror mappings to route requests for specific repositories through a mirror or proxy endpoint'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Configure proxy settings if required', 'detail': 'Set proxy host, port, and authentication for outbound repository access'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Validate configuration', 'detail': 'Run a test build to confirm dependencies resolve from appropriate sources and no circular references exist'}
triggers: Multiple artifact sources required
Repository failover or load distribution needed
Mirror or proxy configuration required
Project dependencies span multiple remote repositories
constraints: Repository endpoints must be reachable and properly authenticated
Mirror and proxy configurations must not create circular references
Repository priority order must be explicitly defined to avoid ambiguity
Credentials for authenticated repositories must be securely stored
cautions: Misconfigured mirrors can cause dependency resolution failures
Proxy timeouts may require tuning for slow network conditions
Repository priority order affects build reproducibility; document rationale
Ensure mirror rules do not inadvertently block access to required repositories
output_contract: Maven settings configured with multiple repository endpoints; build successfully resolves dependencies from appropriate sources in priority order; no unresolved artifact errors; proxy and mirror rules function without circular references

metadata.prompt: Configure Maven settings to enable dependency resolution from multiple repository sources. Define repository endpoints, apply mirror rules, configure proxy settings, and establish priority order for artifact lookup. Verify that the build resolves dependencies from appropriate sources according to configuration.

skill_drafts.name: Secure Remote Repository Access via Authenticated HTTPS
skill_drafts.description: Configuration of credentials and HTTPS authentication for accessing remote Maven repositories with security requirements. Enforces encrypted transport and credential protection when repositories require authentication.
skill_drafts.objective: Enforce secure authenticated access to remote repositories
contraindications: Public unauthenticated repository without credential requirements
HTTP-only repository where encryption is not enforced
No credential management capability available
workflow_steps: Verify repository URL uses HTTPS protocol
Obtain and securely store authentication credentials
Configure credentials in secure credential store or encrypted settings
Establish HTTPS connection to remote repository
Validate certificate and authenticate with provided credentials
Test dependency resolution through authenticated HTTPS channel
Confirm build succeeds with secure artifact access
triggers: Repository requires authentication credentials
HTTPS encryption is mandatory for repository access
Sensitive credentials must be protected during artifact resolution
constraints: HTTPS connection must be established before credential transmission
Credentials must not be stored in plaintext in configuration files
Certificate validation must be enabled for HTTPS connections
cautions: Verify certificate chain validity to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks
Rotate credentials regularly and revoke compromised tokens
Audit credential access and repository connection logs

Compliance or audit requirements demand reproducible builds

Build environment-specific variation is intentional or required

Document all build parameters: compiler version, plugin versions, dependency versions, timestamps
Configure reproducible build properties in pom.xml (e.g., project.build.outputTimestamp)
Update settings.xml to enforce consistent repository mirrors and credentials handling
Execute build in first environment and capture artifact checksums
Execute build in second environment and verify artifact checksums match
Document reproducible build configuration and validation results

Preparing artifacts for release or distribution

Projects without parent-child module relationships
